items.markdown:
If you mean a **blue Staffordshire Bull Terrier (Staffy)**, there are some current listings around Aberdeen/Aberdeenshire, but I’d be quite selective about the breeder rather than choosing purely on colour.

### Where to look

- **The Royal Kennel Club’s Find a Puppy** is the safest starting point. You can filter Staffordshire Bull Terriers by location and, importantly, by whether the parents have been health tested. [royalkennelclub.com](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/find-an-assured-breeder/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?ActiveCertifiedBreeder=False&Breeds=Staffordshire+Bull+Terrier&Distance=15&FemaleDogs=False&GeneralRescueClubs=False&HealthTested=False&MaleDogs=False&SearchRescueClubs=False&SortNearest=False&TotalResults=0&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- I found a current **blue Staffy listing in Aberdeenshire** advertising KC registration and puppies available from 8 weeks. Treat marketplace adverts as leads rather than endorsements, and independently verify the breeder and health certificates. [Staffie-Owners.co.uk](https://www.staffie-owners.co.uk/staffies-for-sale/aberdeenshire?colour=blue&kc_registered=yes&ready_to_leave=now&sex=male&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- There is also a local Aberdeen dog breeder listing, Moonlight Shadow Blue Roan Dogs, although the search result does **not** establish that they currently have blue Staffy puppies, so I wouldn't assume they do.

### What I'd ask the breeder

For a Staffy, these are particularly important:

1. **“Can I see the mother with the puppies?”**
 Visit where the puppies were actually raised. The Royal Kennel Club specifically advises seeing the dam and puppies before committing. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/find-an-assured-breeder/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
2. **“Can I see the parents' actual health-test certificates/results?”**
 For Staffordshire Bull Terriers, ask specifically about:

 - **HC-HSF4 hereditary cataracts DNA test**
- **L-2-HGA DNA test**
- **BVA/KC elbow testing**
- **BVA/KC/ISDS eye testing**, including litter eye screening. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?gad=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com) [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/BreedSpecificRequirements?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

 Don't accept simply “both parents are health tested”—ask to see the results.
3. **“What are the parents like temperament-wise?”**
 Ask about behaviour around people, children and other dogs, and whether either parent has shown fear or aggression.
4. **“What socialisation have the puppies had?”**
 Ask what they've experienced—household noises, handling, visitors, children, grooming, car journeys, other dogs, etc.
5. **“Can I see the puppy's KC registration/pedigree and the parents' details?”**
 KC registration establishes pedigree information, but **it isn't a substitute for health testing**.
6. **“What exactly comes with the puppy?”**
 Ask about microchipping, vaccinations, worming, insurance, food, contract, registration paperwork and vet records.
7. **“How many litters does the mother have, and how old is she?”**
 Ask how frequently she's been bred and whether there have been any complications or health problems in previous litters.
8. **“Why did you choose these two dogs to breed?”**
 A good breeder should be able to explain the health, temperament and pedigree reasoning—not just say they wanted blue puppies.

### One important point about “blue”

I'd put **health and temperament ahead of colour**. The Royal Kennel Club explicitly notes that colour should not take priority over health and temperament when choosing a Staffy. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

If you tell me **how far you're willing to travel from Aberdeen (e.g. 50, 100 or 200 miles)**, I can search for **currently advertised blue Staffy litters and breeders in Scotland/Northern England**, and separate the listings with verifiable health testing from the ones I'd approach cautiously.
